Element of the day: Hydrogen (H, 1).

The universe's most abundant element starts the periodic table. A neutral hydrogen atom has one proton and one electron.

Explore its properties on Elementa:
https://elementalearn.com/element/hydrogen/?utm_source=x&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=element_of_day&utm_content=day01_hydrogen

Element of the day: Helium (He, 2).

Helium was detected in the Sun's spectrum in 1868, before it was confirmed on Earth. Its name comes from Helios, the Sun.

A little astronomy in the periodic table:
https://elementalearn.com/element/helium/?utm_source=x&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=element_of_day&utm_content=day02_helium

Element of the day: Lithium (Li, 3).

A neutral lithium atom has three electrons: two in its first shell and one in its second. That outer electron is a useful clue to its Group 1 chemistry.

Explore Li:
https://elementalearn.com/element/lithium/?utm_source=x&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=element_of_day&utm_content=day03_lithium

Element of the day: Carbon (C, 6).

Diamond and graphite are both forms of pure carbon. Different atomic arrangements give them very different properties.

What else can the same element become?
https://elementalearn.com/element/carbon/?utm_source=x&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=element_of_day&utm_content=day04_carbon

Element of the day: Nitrogen (N, 7).

Nitrogen gas makes up about 78% of Earth's air by volume. Nitrogen compounds also help build the molecules of living things.

Explore the element around us:
https://elementalearn.com/element/nitrogen/?utm_source=x&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=element_of_day&utm_content=day05_nitrogen

Element of the day: Oxygen (O, 8).

Oxygen gas makes up about 21% of Earth's atmosphere by volume. Every oxygen atom has eight protons, whether it's in air, water or a rock.

Explore O on Elementa:
https://elementalearn.com/element/oxygen/?utm_source=x&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=element_of_day&utm_content=day06_oxygen

Element of the day: Neon (Ne, 10).

Pure neon glows reddish orange in a discharge tube. The other colours in signs often come from different gases.

Explore the chemistry behind the glow:
https://elementalearn.com/element/neon/?utm_source=x&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=element_of_day&utm_content=day07_neon

Element of the day: Sodium (Na, 11).

The orange glow of sodium street lamps is a clue to the element inside. Sodium's atomic number is 11, and its neutral atom has one outer-shell electron.

Explore Na:
https://elementalearn.com/element/sodium/?utm_source=x&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=element_of_day&utm_content=day08_sodium

Element of the day: Magnesium (Mg, 12).

Magnesium sits at the centre of chlorophyll, the pigment that helps plants capture light for photosynthesis.

One element connects metals and green leaves:
https://elementalearn.com/element/magnesium/?utm_source=x&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=element_of_day&utm_content=day09_magnesium

Element of the day: Aluminium (Al, 13).

A thin oxide layer helps protect aluminium from further corrosion. Surface chemistry is one reason this light metal is so useful.

Explore Al's properties:
https://elementalearn.com/element/aluminium/?utm_source=x&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=element_of_day&utm_content=day10_aluminium

Element of the day: Silicon (Si, 14).

Silicon is a semiconductor. Tiny amounts of added elements can change its electrical properties, which helps make modern electronics possible.

Meet the element inside the chip:
https://elementalearn.com/element/silicon/?utm_source=x&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=element_of_day&utm_content=day11_silicon

Element of the day: Phosphorus (P, 15).

Phosphate groups help form the backbone of DNA and RNA. They're also part of ATP, which cells use in energy transfer.

Explore the element behind those phosphates:
https://elementalearn.com/element/phosphorus/?utm_source=x&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=element_of_day&utm_content=day12_phosphorus

Element of the day: Sulfur (S, 16).

Sulfur commonly forms yellow crystals or powder. It's also part of amino acids that help build proteins.

Explore the element from minerals to living things:
https://elementalearn.com/element/sulfur/?utm_source=x&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=element_of_day&utm_content=day13_sulfur

Element of the day: Iron (Fe, 26).

Iron is part of haemoglobin, the protein that carries oxygen in your blood. Its chemistry matters in living cells as well as in steel.

Explore Fe on Elementa:
https://elementalearn.com/element/iron/?utm_source=x&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=element_of_day&utm_content=day14_iron
